title: approve asks once: drop the leftover askYes elicitation
description: ADR 0057 (docs/adr/0057-*) says `decide`, `approve` and `accept` take the relayed pick and no longer elicit. `decide` and `accept` were migrated in a2f1d6c, but the `approve` tool in packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts (~line 505) still calls `askYes` after the host's question tool already got a yes — so the human confirms every brief twice. Fix: remove the askYes call and its `if (!yes)` branch; keep the `confirmed: z.literal(true)` input, the no-brief guard, `queueByDefault` resolution, and the queued/non-queued return texts. Drop the `askYes` import from plan.ts only if `edit_decision` (~line 394) no longer uses it — it does today, and edit_decision is out of scope. Update the stale comment in packages/mcp/src/ask.ts if it still lists approve. Also check the `approve` tool description still tells the agent to name the queue outcome in its own question (the old button text 'Yes — approve, and start it when it is ready' carried that; move that hint into the description so the host's question says whether it will auto-start). Check: `pnpm -F @besober/mcp exec tsc --noEmit` (or the repo's typecheck script) passes, and `rg -n askYes packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` shows only the edit_decision call.

brief.approach:
Most of this node is already done and the work left is one sentence. Score 1: a single string in one file, verified by grep.

**What is already true**, checked in the tree today rather than assumed. The `approve` tool in `packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` (the handler now at ~line 496) calls `approveBrief` directly. There is no `askYes` in it and no `if (!yes)` branch — that landed in `6e53283`, node `approve-takes-the-relayed-yes-and-stops-fcbt`. `rg -n askYes packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts` shows exactly one call, at line 396 in `edit_decision`, which the node's own text puts out of scope; the import on line 28 therefore stays. The comment on `askYes` in `packages/mcp/src/ask.ts:95-102` talks about "every approval cost two extra keystrokes" as a historical finding from the M1 gate and does not list `approve` as a current caller, so it is not stale and is not to be edited. The `confirmed: z.literal(true)` input, the no-brief guard, the `queueByDefault` resolution and both return texts are all present and correct.

**What is left.** The old elicitation carried its own button text — `Yes — approve, and start it when it is ready` — and that was the only place the human was told, at the moment of asking, whether saying yes also starts the node. Removing the elicitation removed that sentence and nothing replaced it: the host's own question tool is driven by the agent, and the agent is steered by the tool's `description`. So the outcome has to be named there.

Add one sentence to the `approve` tool's `description` string (`packages/mcp/src/tools/plan.ts`, the `registerTool('approve', …)` block): the question the agent puts to the human must say whether a yes also starts the node when it becomes ready, which is what `queue` resolves to — the explicit `queue` argument when given, otherwise the board's `dispatch.queueByDefault`. Keep it in the register of the descriptions around it: one sentence, no bullet, no example, the ADR 0057 reference at the end left where it is.

Change nothing else: not the `inputSchema`, not the `queue` field's own `.describe()`, not the handler, not the two return strings, not `ask.ts`. A tool description is the agent's only instruction here, so the whole node is that one sentence being present and true.

acceptance.proves: exactly two mentions remain — the import and the one `edit_decision` call — so `approve` elicits nothing and the out-of-scope caller was not touched
approving through the tool still takes the relayed yes, refuses a node with no brief, and returns the queued and non-queued sentences as before
the approve tool's description now tells the agent to say, in its own question, whether a yes also starts the node — the sentence the removed elicitation's button text used to carry
only that one file changed: `ask.ts` was left alone because its comment is a historical note, not a stale list of callers
